reference_answer:
Let I,K be finite index sets, e:I->K a bijection, and O a complex unitary matrix on I. Write U_e for its basis-relabeling matrix, U_e[e(i),i]=1 and all other entries zero; it is a unitary map from C^I to C^K. Define T_e(A)=U_e A U_e†, so T_e(A)[e(i),e(j)]=A[i,j], equivalently T_e(A)[a,b]=A[e^{-1}(a),e^{-1}(b)]. This is the simultaneous pullback along e^{-1} on the two matrix axes.

Conjugate transpose commutes with this SAME-axis relabeling. Entrywise, T_e(A)†[a,b]=conjugate(A[e^{-1}(b),e^{-1}(a)])=T_e(A†)[a,b]; equivalently (U_e A U_e†)†=U_e A† U_e†. Multiplication also commutes: T_e(A)T_e(B)=U_e A(U_e†U_e)B U_e†=U_e AB U_e†=T_e(AB). In entries the contracted label z in K is replaced bijectively by e^{-1}(z) in I. Finally T_e(I_I)=I_K. Therefore
T_e(O)† T_e(O)=T_e(O†)T_e(O)=T_e(O†O)=T_e(I_I)=I_K.
The analogous reverse product is also I_K (or follows for square finite-dimensional isometries); hence the reindexed operator is unitary. This is exactly the same-map algebra-equivalence proof implemented by reindex_unitary.

The question's word 'essential' must be read with its explicit qualification 'for the argument': using the same bijection is what makes this single transformation T_e a unital star-algebra isomorphism between the two square-matrix algebras, commuting with adjoint. It is NOT a necessary condition for the resulting matrix to remain square or unitary. To see the boundary, consider arbitrary bijections e,f:I->K and the two-axis map T_{e,f}(A)=U_e A U_f†. It still gives a square K×K matrix. Its adjoint is T_{f,e}(A†), with the axes exchanged, rather than in general T_{e,f}(A†). Also
T_{e,f}(A)T_{e,f}(B)=U_e A(U_f†U_e)B U_f†,
which is generally not T_{e,f}(AB), and T_{e,f}(I)=U_e U_f† need not be I. Thus one cannot repeat the SAME fixed-map algebra-homomorphism proof when e differs from f.

Unitarity nevertheless survives by a different cancellation:
R=U_e O U_f† implies R†R=U_f O†(U_e†U_e)O U_f†=U_f I_I U_f†=I_K,
and RR†=I_K similarly. More generally the correctly matched transformation rule T_{e,f}(A)T_{f,g}(B)=T_{e,g}(AB) explains how the swapped axes in the adjoint give this cancellation. Consistent contracted indices are needed for composition; that does not require the output and input basis bijections to be equal in a general two-sided relabeling.

For an explicit two-dimensional counterexample to any stronger necessity claim, take O=I_2, e=identity and f=swap. Then U_e=I_2, U_f=X=[[0,1],[1,0]], and R=X is square and unitary despite e!=f. Here T_{e,f}(I)=X!=I and T_{e,f}(I)T_{e,f}(I)=I!=X=T_{e,f}(I*I), displaying failure of the one-map unital/product rules without failure of unitarity. Adjoint commutation with that same map can fail too: for Z=diag(1,-1), T_{e,f}(Z)=ZX has adjoint -ZX, whereas T_{e,f}(Z†)=ZX. In zero- or one-dimensional spaces the same-axis proof still holds; there may simply be no distinct bijections available to instantiate this two-dimensional boundary example.

These comparisons do not replace the original standing hypothesis: the requested proof remains the same-bijection theorem. They correct only an overstatement about why that proof works. The result is exact finite-dimensional complex algebra; it makes no primitive-circuit or finite-bit cost claim and does not by itself preserve a separately chosen clean projected block unless its register/clean basis identifications are transported consistently.

rubric.criterion: Defines simultaneous reindexing by T_e(A)[e(i),e(j)]=A[i,j] and states O†O=I and the goal T_e(O)†T_e(O)=I.
Proves same-axis adjoint commutation, multiplicativity and identity preservation, then uses these to prove unitarity (with finite square dimensions or both unitary identities understood).

Explains SAME is essential to this fixed-map algebra-equivalence proof, not to squareness or unitarity in general. Gives R=U_e O U_f† for independent axes and a valid cancellation/counterexample, explicitly rejecting the old 'not square-compatible' explanation without changing the standing same-axis theorem.

exposition.core_summary: Same-bijection reindexing is a star-preserving algebra equivalence and preserves unitarity. Independent row/column bijections also preserve unitarity by two-sided unitary cancellation; what generally fails is using their fixed two-axis map as a unital multiplicative algebra equivalence.

semantic_steps.claim: Define R=T_e(O) by R[e(i),e(j)]=O[i,j], i.e. pullback along e^{-1} on both axes, with the same finite source/target bases.
For simultaneous reindexing, swapping matrix axes under adjoint leaves the same bijection on each axis, so T_e(O)†=T_e(O†).
The same-axis transformation preserves products by consistently relabeling the contracted index and is unital: T_e(A)T_e(B)=T_e(AB).
Apply the original O†O=I identity, same-map adjoint/product rules and T_e(I)=I to get R†R=I and hence finite-dimensional unitarity.

The same-bijection restriction belongs to this fixed-map algebra-equivalence proof, not a universal necessity for unitarity: independent-axis relabeling remains square/unitary as U_e O U_f†, while its same-map product/identity/adjoint rules can fail.
